resources.string: A serious privacy messenger with real end-to-end encryption by default and built-in censorship bypass. No phone, no email, no ads.
Your identity is a numeric UIN and nothing else. The account isn\'t tied to you. Burn it and start over whenever you want.

Normal messaging goes over the internet, like anywhere else. When there is no network at all, Radio Chat takes over: it finds people near you over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct, and messages hop device to device with no servers involved.
End-to-end encrypted on every message. The server doesn\'t see who\'s writing to whom: the sender\'s identity is sealed inside the envelope, not in the header.
A PIN locks the app and encrypts your message history on-device, with optional fingerprint, plus decoy and wipe PINs for when you\'re forced to unlock.
Online, Away, DND, Invisible, Offline. The classic five, and they actually mean something. Tap your status icon to switch.
RCQ isn\'t one company\'s server. Every server is an independent island, and anyone can run one. Your account lives on the island you pick, and you keep your number if you move.

When the network blocks RCQ, the app routes itself through a relay, disguised as ordinary traffic. The relay network is community-run, and onion routing chains it so no single relay sees both you and your island.

Who can read what I send?

Only the person you sent it to. The text is encrypted on your device and decrypted on theirs, and the island in between carries a sealed envelope it cannot open.\n\nWhat the island does see: that you were online, and who your envelopes were addressed to. What it does not see: what is inside them.
What is an island, and why is there more than one?

An island is a server that holds your mail. RCQ is not one server but many independent ones: ours, other people\u0027s, and yours if you run one.\n\nYour number is issued by an island, so the same number on two islands is two different people — an address is the number AND the island. People on different islands still write to each other, call, and share groups.
What do I do when it stops working?

First find out whether you are being blocked: Settings → Network → Connection diagnostics, and run the full check with your VPN OFF.\n\nIt gives you one line. Send it through Report a bug — that line tells us exactly what is closed on your network, and without it we are guessing.
